Answer: C
Reason: Figure 1 shows subtle right-sided opacities, while Figure 2 demonstrates significant new consolidation in the right middle and lower lung fields. This focal progression of opacity, combined with the clinical presentation of pleuritic pain and crackles 18 days after admission, is most consistent with a superimposed bacterial pneumonia rather than diffuse ARDS, pneumothorax, or pure viral progression.
